description: We’re a team of space and technology enthusiasts joining the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We’re looking for teammates interested in coding, game development, design, or space science. All skill levels are welcome—join us to share ideas, learn together, and build something exciting! 🚀

details:
SpaceNav puts users in mission control, transforming space science into a collaborative, hands-on learning experience. Our browser-based platform connects a 3D Solar System explorer with spacecraft design, trajectory planning, and mission simulation, helping users understand how engineering decisions shape a mission from launch to completion.

Users define objectives, choose destinations, configure spacecraft and instruments, and balance fuel, power, mass, communications, budgets, and mission duration. Teams share mission drafts, assign responsibilities, and agree on operating strategies before testing their plans against challenges such as launch failures, communication blackouts, and resource shortages.

What makes SpaceNav unique is the connection between team decisions and visible consequences. Visual mission replays, telemetry, and event logs show how a plan performs and explain why it succeeds or fails. Users can revise their designs, compare outcomes, and learn through experimentation. Adding a scientific instrument, for example, becomes a practical lesson in balancing discovery against power, storage, and cost.

We built SpaceNav using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, with Three.js powering interactive 3D visualization. Python and Django handle mission planning, simulation, validation, accounts, and saved missions, while SQLite supports local data storage. Astronomy Engine supplies astronomical positions, and numerical solvers support trajectory calculations.

Our team considered accessibility, scientific clarity, browser performance, and different experience levels. Guided lessons support beginners, while customizable spacecraft specifications enable deeper exploration. Calculated trajectories and simplified teaching models are clearly distinguished. SpaceNav aims to make space education more accessible while developing systems thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork—giving learners a place to plan, test, fail, and improve together.
